anatomy.flutter: Nothing — the Flutter checkout has no prose.dart or any widget that styles a block of authored long-form markup; there is no equivalent to shape here, only individually styled Text widgets per screen.
anatomy.web: Prose({ asChild, className, ...props }) is a single thin wrapper — Comp = asChild ? Slot.Root : 'div', rendering <Comp data-slot="prose" className={cn("prose", className)} {...props} /> — with all real structure supplied by the caller's markup (h1-h6, p, ul/ol, blockquote, table, pre/code, figure) inside it.
anatomy.note: origin: web-only. Flutter has no long-form-content component at all; this is a web platform concern (styling raw HTML flow content), which is why there is no Dart source to compare against.

api.flutter: Nothing — no Dart constructor exists for this capability; Flutter text content is composed per-screen from Text/RichText widgets rather than through one named component with a shared API.
api.web: Prose accepts asChild (boolean, default false, swaps the rendered element for Radix Slot.Root so a real <article> can be used) plus every other React.ComponentProps<'div'> prop, forwarded via {...props}; it deliberately sets no `measure`/width prop — the component doc says that belongs to PageContainer width="prose" so there is only one owner of that number.
api.note: origin: web-only, so there is no Flutter API to diverge from; recorded as n/a rather than platform-difference because there is nothing on the Flutter side performing this role to compare against, per the brief's guidance for web-only capabilities.

states.flutter: Nothing — no widget exists, so there is no state model to read from Dart source.
states.web: The component's own doc comment declares the state model explicitly: 'presentational, synchronous. rest — the only state. hover/focus-visible/pressed — N/A for the block; links inside it are real anchors...loading/success/error/disabled — N/A, there is no action. empty — N/A.'
states.note: A block of static content has one state by construction on both platforms (there is no Flutter widget to disagree with); the web doc spells this out explicitly rather than leaving it implicit.

disabled.flutter: Nothing — no widget, no enabled/disabled parameter exists to read.
disabled.web: Prose has no disabled prop, no aria-disabled handling, and no CSS for a disabled variant in styles/typeset.css's .prose rules — the component's own doc lists 'success · error · disabled — N/A, there is no action.'
disabled.note: A static content block is not an action and cannot be disabled on either platform; there is nothing to disable because the component performs no operation.

interaction.flutter: Nothing — no widget exists, so there is no keyboard/pointer/focus handling to compare.
interaction.web: Prose adds no interaction handling of its own — it is a plain div/Slot with a className; any interactivity (link hover/focus) comes from real <a> elements inside it, styled by :where(.prose) a and :where(.prose) a:hover in styles/typeset.css, which is native anchor behaviour, not something Prose implements.
interaction.note: Prose itself is inert; whatever interaction exists belongs to the child anchors it wraps, which get the browser's native focus/keyboard handling for free, matching the doc's claim that Prose 'neither overrides' hover nor the global focus ring.

semantics.flutter: Nothing — no Semantics widget or accessibility node exists for this capability in the Flutter checkout.
semantics.web: Prose renders a plain <div data-slot="prose"> by default (or the caller's own element via asChild/Slot.Root, e.g. <article>) with no ARIA role of its own; accessible structure comes entirely from the real heading/list/table elements the caller puts inside it, each carrying native semantics.
semantics.note: There is no accessibility contract to originate from a wrapper div; asChild lets a caller upgrade to a landmark element like <article> when semantically appropriate, which is the correct web mechanism and has no Flutter analogue to compare against.
